overview: Black takes c4 but cannot keep the pawn, and plays ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...c5 or ...a6 and ...b5 for central counterplay. White regains it with e3 and Bxc4, then castles and plays Qe2, Rd1 and Nc3. Typical middlegames feature an IQP or hanging pawns, with active pieces on both sides. The game is open, positional and not very forcing.

white_ideas.idea: e3, Bxc4, O-O, Qe2 and Nc3 for central pressure
Create an IQP for Black with dxc5 or exploit the hanging pawns

black_ideas.idea: ...a6 and ...b5 to gain queenside space and develop the bishop

Open centre with White d4 pawn against Black's active pieces

character.notes: Positional with open lines but not forcing; neither side takes serious risks.

gambit.notes: The pawn on c4 cannot be kept; it returns with Bxc4.

structure.notes: Open, QGA anchor structure with exchanges on d4.

level.notes: Clear plans, IQP knowledge, moderate memory.
